provenance.notes: Educational reference only. Structural projects require professional load reviews and local permit inspection.

siteSelection.guideline: Avoid low spots. Build on high, sloped ground so surface water flows away from foundations.
A windbreak (trees, fence) is vital on the windward side to reduce heating loads.
Longest wall must face within 15 degrees of true South to maximize passive winter heat.
Ensure clear, level pathways for transport of materials, fuel, and emergency vehicles.
Place close to springs or catchment cistern tanks to limit uphill bucket carrying.
Pitch roofs to 4:12 minimum in heavy snow regions to prevent structural rafter collapse.
Clear all tall brush and combustible materials within a 30-foot perimeter of the structure.

foundations.frost: Requires insulation skirt (FPSF) or deep footings

framingSteps.desc: Laying sill plates on foundation, mounting joists (spaced 16" or 24" on center), and screwing subfloor plywood panels.
Assembling vertical wall frames flat on floor, inserting double headers above door/window openings, and raising walls.
Installing ceiling joists and roof rafters or pre-engineered triangular roof trusses to support roof loads.
Covering wall and roof framing with OSB or plywood sheets, then applying housewrap (vapor-permeable weather barrier).

insulationOptions.pros: Natural, absorbs moisture without losing R-value, filters indoor air.
Fireproof, water repellent, rodent repellent, doesn't settle.
High R-value, blocks moisture, easy to cut.
insulationOptions.cons: Flammable, petroleum-based, releases toxic gas if burned.

insulationOptions.pros: Highly renewable, carbon capturing, superior thermal mass when plastered.
insulationOptions.cons: Thick walls require wide foundations, highly vulnerable to water rot during build.
